# Results — Study 236 (Fifty-Two-Week-High) on real daily tape

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). Signal: 52-week-high
proximity = close / 252d rolling high.  Stocks ranked cross-sectionally by proximity;
Q5 = nearest 52-week high (the momentum long), Q1 = farthest from 52-week high
(the momentum short).  Equal-weight quintile portfolios, forward log-return measured
at 5, 20, and 65 trading days.  Rebalanced every 5 trading days.  Universe: 20
representative S&P 500 large-cap names (AAPL, MSFT, AMZN, GOOGL, META, NVDA, JPM,
JNJ, XOM, PG, V, MA, HD, UNH, CVX, MRK, ABBV, PEP, KO, WMT).
**Survivorship-biased** — all names still trade as of 2026-06-16.
As-of **2026-06-16**.  Panel: 3,384 days × 20 tickers, 2013-01-02 → 2026-06-16.*

## The honest test — Q5-minus-Q1 spread (gross, cost = 0)

Stocks sorted by proximity to 52-week high (ascending), equal-weight quintile
portfolios, forward return over 5 trading days, rebalanced weekly (n = 626 periods).

| Quintile | label | mean return (bps/period) | HAC *t* | ann. return (%) |
|---|---|--:|--:|--:|
| **Q1** | far from 52-week high | **+38.26** | +3.17 | **+13.8%** |
| Q2 | low-intermediate | +38.61 | +4.30 | +13.9% |
| Q3 | middle | +32.81 | +3.58 | +11.8% |
| Q4 | high-intermediate | +20.23 | +2.22 | +7.3% |
| **Q5** | near 52-week high | **+27.66** | +3.55 | **+10.0%** |
| **Q5 − Q1 spread** | momentum long-short | **−10.60** | **−0.85** | — |

**Key finding:** Q1 (far from the 52-week high) *outperforms* Q5 (near the 52-week
high) at the 5-day horizon.  The Q5-Q1 spread is **negative** at this horizon —
the momentum thesis is wrong in direction on this large-cap survivorship-biased sample —
and statistically insignificant (HAC *t* = −0.85).

This contradicts the George-Hwang (2004) result, which was found on a broader,
less biased mid-to-large-cap universe over a longer historical period (1963-2001).
On this 20-name survivorship-biased panel, large-cap names near their highs (NVDA,
AAPL, META in momentum regimes) carry high valuations and subsequently mean-revert,
while names that have fallen from highs within this elite group tend to recover.

## Hold-period sweep (Q5-Q1 spread, gross)

| Hold period | spread (bps/period) | HAC *t* | n periods |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 1 day | **+10.54** | **+1.57** | 627 |
| 5 days | −10.60 | −0.85 | 626 |
| 10 days | −32.11 | −1.39 | 625 |
| 20 days | −60.71 | −1.42 | 623 |
| 65 days | −139.13 | −1.39 | 614 |

Only the 1-day horizon shows a positive (momentum-consistent) spread, but it does
not breach |*t*| ≥ 2.  At all longer horizons the spread is negative and all remain
below the inference bar.  None of these crosses |*t*| ≥ 2.

## Long-only comparison: top decile vs equal-weight baseline (5-day hold)

| Arm | mean (bps/period) | ann. return | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| Top decile (near 52w-high) | +18.83 | +6.8%/yr | +2.11 |
| Equal-weight basket (baseline) | +31.51 | +11.3%/yr | +4.26 |
| Spread (top − baseline) | **−12.68** | — | **−1.62** |

A long-only investor buying the 10% of names closest to their 52-week highs would
have earned **+6.8%/yr** against a **+11.3%/yr** equal-weight baseline — a drag
of 4.5 percentage points per year, before any transaction costs.

## Survivorship bias note

The universe is locked to 20 names that are all current S&P 500 constituents and
still trade in 2026.  This introduces a specific selection bias: stocks admitted
to this basket are companies with proven long-term track records.  Within this elite
group, names that have fallen from their 52-week highs are "temporarily soft" high-
quality companies — not genuine losers — which biases Q1 *upward* relative to an
unbiased universe.  The George-Hwang anomaly was documented on a broader universe
that includes genuinely poor-quality laggard stocks in Q1 (the momentum short leg).

## Synthetic positive control — the engine knows the difference

On a deterministic synthetic panel, the Q5-Q1 spread is monotone in the planted
AR(1) momentum coefficient, confirming the engine is a faithful detector:

| Planted AR(1) | description | spread (bps) | HAC *t* |
|---|---|--:|--:|
| −0.40 | strong reversion | negative | large negative |
| 0.00 | martingale | ~0 | ~0 |
| +0.40 | strong momentum | positive | large positive |

The real tape sits in a regime where, within this elite large-cap basket, the
near-high quintile *underperforms* — indicating the survivorship-biased sample
inverts the originally documented anomaly.

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** Q5-Q1 spread = −10.60 bps/period, HAC *t* = −0.85;
  statistically indistinguishable from zero and *in the wrong direction* for the
  momentum thesis on this specific large-cap survivorship-biased sample.  No hold
  period from 1 to 65 days crosses the |*t*| ≥ 2 inference bar.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** The top decile earns only +6.8%/yr against a
  +11.3%/yr passive baseline before any costs.  Adding realistic transaction costs
  makes it an outright underperformer.
- **Sample scope caveat.** The George-Hwang (2004) anomaly was documented on
  1963-2001 data across the broader CRSP universe.  The 2013-2026 large-cap
  survivorship-biased sample used here is not the right test bed for the original
  claim.  The signal may exist in a broader, unbiased, longer-horizon universe.
